item.text: {"search_note":"Strongest evidence is for disasters and conflict-related suffering: hurricane response, Gaza civilian protection, and de-escalation diplomacy. I found no strong direct 2024 pandemic-specific evidence and very little famine-specific evidence. The biggest counterevidence is the Gaza accountability gap: Biden pressed for protection and ceasefire, but follow-through on civilian-harm incidents was weak. Ukraine policy is mixed: some steps were defensively framed, but they still expanded escalation risk, so they are not clean harm-reduction evidence.","evidence":[{"title":"FACT SHEET: Biden-Harris Administration Approves Nearly $2 Billion for Hurricane Response, Recovery, and Resilience in Response to Hurricanes Helene and Milton","publisher":"The American Presidency Project / White House","date":"2024-10-16","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/fact-sheet-biden-harris-administration-approves-nearly-2-billion-for-hurricane-response","summary":"The administration prioritized temporary housing, food, water, emergency supplies, debris removal, and infrastructure restoration.
